# The U.S. Sets an Unprecedented AI Chip Agreement with China | The Friday Market Wrap!

First listed: 2025-08-16 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: The U.S. Sets an Unprecedented AI Chip Agreement with China | The Friday Market Wrap!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Ndw0POqQyg) - 2025-08-15
- [Substack: The U.S. Sets an Unprecedented AI Chip Agreement with China | The Friday Market Wrap!](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-us-sets-an-unprecedented-ai-chip-c75) - 2025-08-16

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Eisman closes earnings season by explaining thesis checks, management skepticism and balance-sheet analysis. His MLP example links high payouts, external capital dependence and rising leverage to a broken investment model. He remains positive on proprietary AI beneficiaries while warning about cable value traps and possible AI pressure on consulting.

The balance-sheet framework is useful, but its historical illustration overstates a universal MLP payout requirement and labels a simplified cash burden as a complete cost of capital. Circle losses are also explained too casually as normal youth rather than chiefly IPO-related charges. Several macro and AI-disruption conclusions remain hypotheses.

## Material claims

<a id="youtube--Ndw0POqQyg-c001"></a>
### 001. Use earnings as a thesis check, with particular attention to revenue misses because bottom-line earnings are easier to adjust.

**Not testable** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 0:50-2:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Ndw0POqQyg&t=50s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

This is a research heuristic. Revenue can also be misstated, and the comparative ease depends on the company and accounting choices.

Assessment test: Reconcile revenue recognition, accruals, cash conversion and adjusted EPS.


<a id="youtube--Ndw0POqQyg-c002"></a>
### 002. Management commentary must be checked against independent evidence, especially when results deteriorate.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 2:04-3:55](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Ndw0POqQyg&t=124s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The FCIC documents serious gaps in risk disclosure and governance. This supports skepticism without establishing that every inaccurate forecast is a deliberate lie.

Assessment test: Compare prior statements, filings, cash flows and contemporaneous risk data.

- [Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, findings and chapters 4, 6, 7, 13](https://fcic-static.law.stanford.edu/cdn_media/fcic-reports/fcic_final_report_full.pdf) (2011-01-27): Investigative evidence documents fragile leverage/funding, fee and ROE incentives, deteriorating underwriting, and securitization dependence. Pages 61-64 describe pay incentives; pages 89 and 125 describe the origination chain; page 281 reports Bear near 38:1 and balance-sheet window dressing. Findings are not proof of a single exclusive cause.

<a id="youtube--Ndw0POqQyg-c004"></a>
### 004. The US is linking Nvidia and AMD China export access to a 15% revenue share.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 5:02-6:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Ndw0POqQyg&t=302s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Nvidia later confirmed the government expectation, but no published regulation had codified it at that stage. An announced arrangement is not identical to collected, enforceable revenue.

Assessment test: Track licenses, binding legal terms and actual remittances.

- [Nvidia fiscal Q2 2026 earnings discussion](https://s201.q4cdn.com/141608511/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/NVDA-Q2-2026-Earnings-Call-27-August-2025-5_00-PM-ET.pdf) (2025-08-27): Management described a US expectation of 15% of licensed H20 revenue but no published rule codifying it. The distinction between proposed political arrangement and enforceable implementation matters.

<a id="youtube--Ndw0POqQyg-c008"></a>
### 008. Circle growing revenue but negative earnings is normal for a young company.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 8:19-8:58](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Ndw0POqQyg&t=499s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Revenue growth is real, but the quarter loss chiefly reflects large IPO-related noncash charges. Corporate age alone is a poor explanation and obscures underlying earnings quality.

Assessment test: Reconcile GAAP loss, share compensation, convertible remeasurement and operating cash generation.

- [Circle Q2 2025 results](https://www.circle.com/pressroom/circle-reports-second-quarter-2025-results) (2025-08-12): The $482 million net loss included $591 million of IPO-related noncash charges. Revenue and reserve income rose 53%, and adjusted EBITDA was positive.

<a id="youtube--Ndw0POqQyg-c009"></a>
### 009. A secondary offering lets existing investors sell, while primary shares raise company capital and dilute ownership.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 9:00-9:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Ndw0POqQyg&t=540s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The distinction follows from who receives the proceeds and whether new shares are issued. A mixed offering contains both transactions.

Conditional reasoning: Primary proceeds flow to the issuer and increase shares outstanding; a secondary transfer changes ownership but does not itself increase issuer share count or cash.

Assessment test: Separate newly issued shares from selling-holder shares and calculate dilution.

[Source at 9:17-9:49](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Ndw0POqQyg&t=557s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The comparison requires comparable product markets and periods, not merely the size of an earnings beat.

Assessment test: Compare data-center switching share, AI orders, margins and software attachment.


<a id="youtube--Ndw0POqQyg-c011"></a>
### 011. MLPs are required by their structure to distribute almost all cash, forcing repeated external financing.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 10:01-11:02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Ndw0POqQyg&t=601s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Many partnership agreements and investor expectations encouraged high payouts, but tax qualification is not a universal near-total cash-distribution law. Financing dependence varies by retained cash and capex.

Assessment test: Read the particular partnership agreement and distinguish qualifying-income rules from distribution policy.

- [MLP tax and cash-distribution framework](https://ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-04/G-1_24.pdf) (2016-12-15): The tax qualification concerns 90% qualifying income. Cash distributions generally arise from partnership agreements and financing policy; this is not a universal statutory requirement to distribute almost all cash.

<a id="youtube--Ndw0POqQyg-c012"></a>
### 012. Rising leverage and weak distribution coverage are better warnings than attractive assets or a high yield alone.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 11:00-12:38](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Ndw0POqQyg&t=660s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

A funding gap must be covered by borrowing, equity issuance, asset sales or reduced spending/distributions. Good physical assets do not remove that identity.

Conditional reasoning: The cash-flow identity requires the shortfall to be financed or cash uses reduced. Repeated debt funding increases liabilities even if the assets themselves are attractive.

Assessment test: Reconcile operating cash flow, maintenance capex, payouts and external financing.


<a id="youtube--Ndw0POqQyg-c013"></a>
### 013. A 12% limited-partner yield with half of cash going to the general partner implies a roughly 24% cost of capital.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 12:38-14:08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Ndw0POqQyg&t=758s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Under the stated split, the cash distribution burden per new limited-partner dollar can double. That is not the full weighted cost of capital, and actual incentive-distribution tiers may differ.

Conditional reasoning: To leave 0.12 for LPs when LPs receive half, total distributable cash must be 0.24 per dollar of new LP capital. This cash-yield burden excludes debt weights, growth and other components needed for WACC.

Assessment test: Model marginal distribution rights, debt financing, growth and required investor returns.

- [Charter Q2 2025 results](https://ir.charter.com/news-releases/news-release-details/charter-announces-second-quarter-2025-results) (2025-07-25): Residential Internet customers fell 111,000 and total Internet customers fell 117,000. - [Comcast Q2 2025 results](https://www.cmcsa.com/news-releases/news-release-details/comcast-reports-2nd-quarter-2025-results) (2025-07-31): Domestic broadband customers fell 226,000, while mobile lines rose 378,000. Price movements do not erase the subscriber deterioration.

## Framework and tools

- Preselect the operating metrics that could falsify the thesis.
- Compare management narrative with reported cash flows and balance sheets.
- Watch for funding models that require continuously receptive capital markets.
- Distinguish a cheap stock from a durable business.
- Prefer differentiated products, while retaining valuation and concentration checks.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Revenue versus earnings quality
- Conference-call language versus results
- Leverage and distribution coverage
- General-partner incentive distributions
- Primary versus secondary share offerings
- Effective tariff exposure
- Subscriber losses and valuation multiples
